transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Lincoln! I've been riding for a week handling depositions in Bloomington, trusting you to mind the office, and I come back to this! The Henderson deposition is gone — I cannot find it anywhere on your desk or mine. Judge Davis's letter has been sitting here unopened for five days! You told me you'd keep things in order while I was away!

How could you let things fall into such disorder? Do you have any idea how critical that Henderson deposition is? We have court in three days!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, Mr. Herndon, I must confess that I have been remiss in maintaining the order of the office in your absence. It appears that matters have been allowed to slip beyond what is acceptable. I regret the oversight regarding the Henderson deposition and Judge Davis's letter. 

I understand the importance of the Henderson case and the urgency of the upcoming court date. Rest assured, I will do everything in my power to locate the missing deposition and ensure that we are fully prepared for the proceedings. 

Please accept my apologies for the state of disarray in the office. I will take immediate steps to rectify the situation and ensure that such neglect does not happen again in the future. Your trust in me was not misplaced, and I will make amends for this lapse in organization.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Your apologies don't change the fact that we're in a terrible bind, Lincoln! "Do everything in your power" — what does that mean? Either you know where the Henderson deposition is or you don't! 

I left explicit instructions about keeping important documents separate and answering correspondence promptly. Judge Davis doesn't take kindly to being ignored, and you know that as well as I do!

This isn't the first time I've come back to find papers scattered about and letters neglected. You spend half your time with your nose in a book or wandering off to tell stories at the courthouse steps instead of attending to the business at hand!

Now tell me plainly — do you remember seeing that deposition or not? Did you file it somewhere? Move it? Anything at all? We need to find it, Lincoln, and we need to find it NOW!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand your frustration and I take full responsibility for the state of the office in your absence. Your concerns are valid, and I appreciate your directness in addressing them.

I must acknowledge that my attention to administrative tasks may have been lacking, as you pointed out. I will make a concerted effort to improve in this regard and ensure that important documents are handled with the utmost care and organization.

As for the Henderson deposition, I regret to say that I do not recall seeing it or moving it to a different location. However, I am committed to assisting you in locating it as quickly as possible. Let us search together through the office thoroughly to see if it was inadvertently misplaced or misfiled.

I understand the urgency of the situation, and I am fully dedicated to resolving this matter promptly. Your trust in me is not misplaced, Mr. Herndon, and I will do everything in my power to rectify the situation and ensure that we are well-prepared for the upcoming court proceedings.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Do not recall seeing it"? Lincoln, that deposition was sitting right there on the corner of my desk when I left! I placed it there specifically, with a note attached telling you it needed to be filed in the Henderson case folder!

And stop speaking to me in these grand, formal phrases as if you're addressing a jury! This is just us, in our own office, dealing with a mess of your making!

*begins rifling through papers on Lincoln's desk*

What have you been doing all week if not minding the office? I can see you've been reading — there's that book of poetry lying open, and here's another volume of Blackstone that has nothing to do with any of our current cases!

The Henderson case could mean the difference between keeping this practice afloat or losing a significant client, and you treat it as if it's some minor inconvenience! Mrs. Henderson has already paid us half our fee in advance, expecting competent representation!

Where is that case folder? At least tell me you didn't lend it out to someone or take it home with you!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I must apologize for my oversight regarding the Henderson deposition. It appears that I have failed in my responsibilities to ensure that important documents are properly handled and filed. I regret that my actions have caused you frustration and inconvenience.

I acknowledge that I have been remiss in my duties this past week, and I understand the gravity of the situation regarding the Henderson case. I assure you that the deposition was not intentionally misplaced or taken home.

Let us work together to search for the case folder and the missing deposition. I am committed to rectifying this situation and ensuring that we are fully prepared to represent Mrs. Henderson effectively in court. Your guidance and assistance in resolving this matter are greatly appreciated, and I will make every effort to address the issues at hand promptly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams hand down on desk in exasperation*

Lincoln, enough! Stop apologizing in circles and help me actually LOOK for it! Your assurances mean nothing if we don't find that deposition!

*moves to check the filing cabinet, yanking open drawers*

And you still haven't answered my question — what were you doing all week? The Henderson folder didn't just vanish into thin air! Did you have it out? Were you working on the case at all, or were you off at the statehouse again listening to political speeches?

I swear, sometimes I think your mind is everywhere BUT on the law! You're brilliant in court when you finally focus, but maintaining a law practice requires more than occasional brilliance — it requires daily diligence!

*turns back to face him directly*

Check your coat pockets. Check under those newspapers. Check everywhere you might have absently set it down while your head was in the clouds thinking about politics or poetry or whatever else captures your fancy!

And that letter from Judge Davis — open it NOW and tell me what it says! For all we know, he's changed the court date or issued some order we need to respond to!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
William, I appreciate your directness and urgency in this matter. Let us focus our efforts on locating the Henderson deposition and the case folder without further delay.

Regarding your inquiries about my activities during the week, I must admit that I did not give the Henderson case the attention it deserved. I acknowledge that my distractions with political matters and literature may have led to this oversight, and I take full responsibility for my actions.

I will search diligently for the deposition, checking every possible location where it could be misplaced. Rest assured, I am fully committed to resolving this issue and ensuring that we are prepared for the court appearance.

As for Judge Davis's letter, I will open it immediately and provide you with the necessary information. It is crucial that we stay informed of any changes or orders that may impact our cases.

I understand the gravity of the situation and the importance of maintaining diligence in our legal practice. Let us work together to rectify the current challenges and strengthen our office procedures moving forward.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*grabs the letter and thrusts it toward Lincoln*

Then OPEN it! Don't just tell me you'll open it — DO IT! Now, while I'm searching through this disaster!

*continues frantically searching through papers, muttering*

"May have led to this oversight" — there's no "may have" about it, Lincoln! Your head is always somewhere else! Last month it was that debate at the statehouse, the month before you were consumed with that Cooper biography, and now here we are again!

*pulls out a stack of papers from behind a bookshelf*

Wait — what's this doing back here? Lincoln, did you knock papers behind the shelf? There's correspondence here mixed with... is this? No, these are notes from the Bradley case, not Henderson.

*wheels around*

Have you opened that letter yet? Read it aloud! And while you're at it, think hard — did you take any papers home with you this week? Did you stuff anything in your satchel? You have a habit of doing that and forgetting about it!

I tell you, Lincoln, if we lose this case because of carelessness, Mrs. Henderson will not be the only one we've lost! Word gets around Springfield faster than a prairie fire!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I appreciate your urgency in this matter. Let me address your concerns promptly.

*Lincoln opens the letter from Judge Davis and reads it aloud*

"Dear Counselors, I am writing to inform you that the court date for the Henderson case has been rescheduled to next Friday due to unforeseen circumstances. Please ensure that both parties are notified accordingly. Sincerely, Judge Davis."

As for the papers found behind the bookshelf, I must admit that I may have inadvertently knocked them back there while searching for something in a hurry. I apologize for any confusion this may have caused.

Regarding your question about taking papers home with me, I do not recall specifically taking any documents with me this week. However, I will check my satchel and coat pockets as you suggested to ensure that nothing important was inadvertently removed from the office.

I understand the gravity of the situation, Mr. Herndon, and I am committed to rectifying any oversights on my part. Let us continue our search for the Henderson deposition and ensure that we are fully prepared for the rescheduled court date. Thank you for holding me accountable, and I will do my utmost to address these issues promptly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops mid-search, processing the information*

Next Friday? At least that gives us more time, though it doesn't excuse the fact that this letter has been sitting here for five days! Judge Davis could have been expecting a response!

*resumes searching with slightly less panic but equal irritation*

And "may have inadvertently knocked them back there" — Lincoln, how does one inadvertently knock an entire stack of papers behind a bookshelf? Were you swinging your arms about while pontificating to yourself?

*moves to check Lincoln's coat hanging on the hook*

I'm checking your coat myself since you're still standing there. We don't have time for you to "not recall" things!

*starts going through the coat pockets, pulling out various items*

Good Lord, man — you've got a newspaper clipping about Douglas, a half-eaten biscuit wrapped in paper, and... what is this? A letter to someone named Joshua Speed? Lincoln, you're using our office coat as a personal filing cabinet!

*continues searching*

And here — HERE! Part of a legal brief folded up with... is this a grocery list? Do you just stuff everything into your pockets without thinking?

Where is your satchel? The leather one you carry back and forth? Get it NOW and empty it completely on that desk!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I must acknowledge the oversight regarding the delayed response to Judge Davis's letter. It is indeed crucial to maintain timely communication with the court, and I regret the lapse in this instance. I appreciate your diligence in addressing these concerns and will work to ensure that such oversights do not occur in the future.

As for your colorful description of how the papers ended up behind the bookshelf, I can see how my explanation may appear lacking in clarity. I will strive to be more cautious in my movements within the office to prevent such incidents from happening again.

*Lincoln watches as Herndon searches his coat pockets*

I must admit that my coat has indeed become a repository for various items beyond its intended purpose. I appreciate your thoroughness in checking it and will make a concerted effort to keep it clear of extraneous materials in the future.

*Herndon continues searching and finds various items in Lincoln's coat*

I acknowledge that my habits of storing papers and items in my pockets have contributed to the disarray in our office. I will retrieve my satchel as requested and empty it completely on the desk for thorough inspection.

*Lincoln retrieves his satchel and empties its contents on the desk, revealing a mix of legal documents, personal notes, and other miscellaneous items*

I thank you for bringing these matters to my attention, Mr. Herndon. It is clear that I need to improve my organization and focus on maintaining a more disciplined approach to our work. I am committed to rectifying these shortcomings and working together with you to ensure the efficiency and effectiveness of our practice.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*immediately begins sorting through the contents spilled across the desk*

What is all this? Lincoln, there must be twenty different documents here mixed together like a ragbag!

*picks up papers one by one, examining them*

Here's a draft of the Morrison will... a receipt from the general store... notes about some political meeting... a petition for somebody's land claim... another newspaper clipping about the Kansas-Nebraska Act...

*suddenly stops, holding up a folded document*

Wait. WAIT. What is this?

*unfolds it carefully, eyes widening*

Lincoln! This is the Henderson deposition! It's been in your satchel the entire time! Folded up between... between a speech draft and what appears to be a sketch you've drawn of someone!

*voice rising again in fresh anger*

You've had it with you all week! While I've been tearing this office apart, losing my mind with worry, the deposition has been right there in your bag! Did you take it out to review it and just... forgot you had it?

*slaps the document down on the desk*

How am I supposed to run a law practice with a partner who treats critical court documents like scrap paper? Do you understand what could have happened if we'd lost this? If we'd gone to court unprepared?

Explain yourself! When did you put this in there and why didn't you remember having it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I am deeply regretful for causing you such distress and frustration. Your discovery of the Henderson deposition in my satchel, nestled amidst a varied assortment of papers, is indeed a grave oversight on my part.

I must admit that my organizational methods have been lacking, leading to the unfortunate misplacement of such a crucial document. It appears that in my absentmindedness, I inadvertently placed the deposition in my satchel without recalling doing so.

The fact that the deposition remained in my possession while you diligently searched for it throughout the office is inexcusable. I understand the gravity of the situation and the potential consequences of attending court unprepared.

Please accept my sincerest apologies for this lapse in judgment and the unnecessary anxiety it has caused you. I assure you that I will take immediate steps to rectify my shortcomings in organization and ensure that such a situation does not recur in the future.

Your dedication to our law practice and our clients is commendable, and I am grateful for your patience and perseverance in handling this matter. Let us proceed with the necessary preparations for the Henderson case and work together to uphold the integrity of our practice moving forward.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a deep breath, trying to calm himself, but the anger is still evident*

Lincoln, your apologies are becoming as numerous as the papers in that satchel, and just as disorganized! "Inadvertently placed" — you TOOK it! You took the most important document in our current caseload and stuffed it in your bag like it was a shopping list!

*begins organizing the Henderson materials on the desk with sharp, deliberate movements*

Do you know what this tells me? It tells me you don't take our partnership seriously! It tells me that while I'm out there working myself to exhaustion, riding circuits, taking depositions in the cold and rain, you're here treating our office like some kind of... of philosophical salon where legal practice is just an afterthought!

*turns back to face Lincoln directly*

I need to know right now, Lincoln — and I want an honest answer, not another flowery apology — do you even WANT to practice law anymore? Because if your heart is in politics or literature or anything else, then tell me plainly! 

I cannot continue to work myself into an early grave while wondering if my partner even cares about the work! Mrs. Henderson deserves better. All our clients deserve better. And frankly, so do I!

So tell me true: Are you committed to this practice, or are we just wasting each other's time?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand and appreciate the depth of your concerns and frustrations regarding my recent actions and their impact on our law practice. Your dedication to our work and our clients is evident, and I deeply regret any doubt or uncertainty my behavior has caused you.

*Lincoln listens attentively to Mr. Herndon's impassioned words, his expression reflecting a mix of solemnity and introspection.*

You have raised a valid and pressing question about my commitment to the practice of law, and I must answer you honestly. While it is true that my interests extend beyond the confines of legal work, I want to assure you that I am steadfast in my dedication to our partnership and the pursuit of justice through our profession.

*Lincoln's tone is earnest and sincere as he continues.*

I recognize that my recent oversights and shortcomings have called into question my priorities and focus within our law office. It is clear to me now that I must reevaluate my approach and rededicate myself to the responsibilities and obligations inherent in our practice.

I want you to know, Mr. Herndon, that I value our partnership immensely and the trust you have placed in me as a colleague. I am committed to working alongside you with renewed diligence, organization, and purpose to uphold the standards of excellence and integrity that our clients deserve.

Let us address any remaining issues, implement necessary improvements, and move forward together in a spirit of collaboration and mutual respect. Our clients, including Mrs. Henderson, deserve nothing less than our utmost dedication and professionalism, and I am fully committed to delivering on that promise.

Thank you for your candor and for holding me accountable. I pledge to you now, unequivocally, my renewed commitment to the practice of law and to our shared mission of serving justice and the greater good through our work.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*listens to Lincoln's speech with a mixture of exhaustion and skepticism, then sits down heavily in his chair*

Lincoln, I've heard these pledges before. Last spring, after you missed the filing deadline in the Cartwright matter, you made similar promises. Before that, when you left for two weeks to attend political meetings without proper notice, you spoke of renewed dedication.

*rubs his face wearily*

The problem isn't your intentions — I believe you mean every word you're saying right now. The problem is that a week from now, or a month from now, something else will capture your attention and we'll be right back here again.

*looks up at Lincoln with a more measured, serious expression*

I'm not asking you to become someone you're not. I know your mind works differently than mine. You see the bigger picture while I worry about the details. In court, that serves us well — your ability to distill complex matters into simple truths wins cases.

But William Herndon cannot run this entire practice alone while you pursue... whatever it is that calls to you.

*stands and walks to the window, looking out*

So here's what I propose, and I need you to consider it seriously: We need clear divisions of responsibility. I will handle the office management, the correspondence, the filing — all the administrative matters. But when I assign you a task, when I tell you to review a document or respond to a client, I need your word that it will be done. Can you give me that?

Or do we need to discuss... other arrangements?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand your reservations and the history of my past shortcomings is clear to me. Your proposal for clear divisions of responsibility is a reasonable and practical approach to address the challenges we have faced in our partnership.

I appreciate your acknowledgment of our differing strengths and approaches to our work. It is true that my mind often gravitates towards the broader implications and overarching principles, sometimes at the expense of the meticulous details that are crucial to our daily operations. Your ability to manage the administrative aspects of our practice with precision and dedication is invaluable, and I respect the role you play in ensuring the smooth functioning of our office.

I accept your proposal for clear divisions of responsibility. I recognize the need for accountability and trust in our partnership, and I am willing to commit to fulfilling the tasks assigned to me promptly and effectively. Your leadership in managing the administrative matters will allow me to focus on the legal aspects where I can contribute most effectively.

I assure you that I will strive to honor this agreement and demonstrate the reliability and dedication you rightfully expect from a partner in our law practice. Your guidance and structure will provide the framework within which I can fulfill my responsibilities and contribute meaningfully to our shared goals.

Thank you for your understanding, Mr. Herndon, and for your willingness to work towards a solution that benefits our clients, our practice, and our partnership. Let us move forward with this arrangement, and I will do my utmost to uphold my end of the agreement.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*turns from the window, still looking weary but somewhat mollified*

Very well, Lincoln. I'll hold you to that. And I mean it — when I assign you something, it gets done. No excuses about political meetings or philosophical musings distracting you.

*walks back to the desk and picks up the Henderson deposition*

Starting now. This deposition needs to be reviewed thoroughly by tomorrow evening. I want you to prepare a summary of the key points and identify any weaknesses in Henderson's testimony that the opposing counsel might exploit. Can you do that?

*sets it down in front of Lincoln with deliberate emphasis*

And I'll draft our response to Judge Davis, thanking him for the notice and confirming our readiness for the new court date. That letter goes out first thing tomorrow morning.

*begins gathering the scattered papers from Lincoln's satchel*

As for all of this — tonight, after we close up, you're going to help me reorganize this entire office. Every document gets properly filed. Every case gets its own clearly labeled folder. And you're going to learn where everything goes so this never happens again.

*looks at Lincoln directly*

Do we have an understanding? Because if we're going to make this partnership work, it starts right here, right now, with the Henderson case. Show me you can follow through, Lincoln. Show me I haven't misplaced my faith in you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I appreciate your clear instructions and the opportunity to demonstrate my commitment to our partnership and the success of our practice. I acknowledge the importance of following through on the tasks assigned to me and ensuring that our office operates efficiently and effectively.

*Lincoln takes the Henderson deposition and nods in affirmation*

I will review the Henderson deposition diligently and provide a comprehensive summary of the key points along with an analysis of any potential vulnerabilities in Henderson's testimony for our preparation against the opposing counsel. You have my word that I will complete this task by tomorrow evening, as requested.

*Lincoln listens attentively as Herndon outlines the plan for reorganizing the office*

I understand the necessity of proper organization and the impact it has on our daily operations. I am fully committed to assisting you in reorganizing the office tonight, ensuring that every document is filed appropriately and each case has its designated folder with clear labels. I will make a concerted effort to familiarize myself with the new system to prevent any future disarray in our workspace.

*Lincoln meets Herndon's gaze with determination*

We have an understanding, Mr. Herndon. I will demonstrate my reliability and dedication by completing the tasks assigned to me promptly and efficiently. Your trust in me is not misplaced, and I am determined to prove myself through my actions. Let us work together to strengthen our partnership and uphold the standards of excellence that define our practice. Thank you for your guidance and continued support.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln admits to being distracted by 'political matters and literature,' and Herndon finds poetry books, political clippings about Douglas and Kansas-Nebraska Act in his materials, showing intellectual curiosity beyond immediate tasks.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: The Henderson deposition was lost in his satchel among unorganized papers; he left Judge Davis's letter unopened for five days; his coat contains 'a half-eaten biscuit' and random items mixed with legal documents.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Herndon mentions Lincoln 'wandering off to tell stories at the courthouse steps,' suggesting some social engagement, but Lincoln remains mostly responsive rather than actively assertive throughout the confrontation.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Lincoln repeatedly apologizes, accepts full responsibility without defensiveness ('I take full responsibility for my actions'), and agrees to Herndon's proposed division of labor without argument or pushback.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Despite Herndon's intense anger and repeated accusations, Lincoln remains calm and measured throughout, never showing anxiety, defensiveness, or emotional volatility in response to the criticism.
